title: KMS origin verification and RBACv2 tenant-claim migration
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Enforce and validate KMS origin provenance for tenant-scoped keys and migrate RBACv2 policy mappings to include a canonical tenant claim (kms_origin). Motivation: Several incidents and audit reviews identified ambiguous KMS usage where resources created under cross-tenant key aliases could bypass region pinning and audit attributions. This PR introduces a runtime verifier, schema additions, policy mapping changes, and a migration path to avoid any data residency or key provenance regressions.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds server-side KMS origin verification middleware that checks a signed KMS metadata header (X-Redwood-KMS-Origin) and rejects requests where the origin does not match the tenant's allowed KMS origins.
- Extends RBACv2 policy principal mapping to surface a new attribute `tenant.kms_origin` that policy authors can target for allow/deny rules. The policy compiler was updated to emit attribute checks.
- Adds an audit envelope field `kms_origin` into signed audit records and ensures the audit forwarder populates provenance before sealing.
- Includes a migration/backfill script to populate `tenant.kms_origin` for existing resources using recorded KMS usage and CMK tags. The script is idempotent and runs in canary batches.
- Updates private installer and Helm validation to surface configuration errors when KMS origins are missing for tenants with region pin rules.

Rollback & rollout plan:
- Change gated behind feature flag `rbacv2.kms_origin_enforcement`. Default OFF on main.
- Backfill run as a separate Canary job (scripts/migrations/backfill_kms_origin.py) and validated via smoke checks before enabling enforcement.
- Fallback policy: if enforcement is enabled and verification fails, requests are either rejected or routed to a configurable fallback policy (default: reject).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for verifier and policy compiler changes
- [x] Integration tests updating auth flow with KMS-origin header
- [x] Migration script added with dry-run mode
- [x] Docs: security/kms-origins.md + console messaging for tenant admins
- [x] Helm/installer validation updated

Notes on scope: This change touches the core authorization path and audit pipeline. It does not change encryption primitives or CMK rotation behavior. The intent is provenance enforcement only.

References: Linear ENG-4621, SEC-213, prior incident notes (link redacted), and RFC: kms-origin-provenance-v1 (internal).

release_notes: Security: add KMS origin verification and RBACv2 tenant.kms_origin attribute. Migration: backfill script provided. Rollout gated behind feature flag rbacv2.kms_origin_enforcement. No encryption changes; this enforces provenance and audit attribution.
notes_for_ops: Before enabling enforcement in production: 1) run backfill in dry-run against staging; 2) confirm canary tenants show 0 unexpected rejections; 3) ensure tenant admins have configured allowed KMS origins via Console or API. If unexpected rejections occur, toggle feature flag off and investigate audit logs (field kms_origin in envelopes).
